More importantly, S1 describes a CPU-side conversion process (O(W*H*D) complexity) which is not inherently 'efficient' in terms of computational load compared to GPU-side processing, though the resulting texture allows for efficient sampling. The claim mixes attributes from both sources without clear distinction. S1 supports the legacy/fixed-function aspect well. S2 supports the shader/efficiency aspect. The claim combines them into a single statement about 'the evidence'. Since S1 does not support 'efficient hardware sampling' as a primary strength (it focuses on the conversion overhead and legacy compatibility), and S2 does not support 'legacy OpenGL fixed-function' (it focuses on shaders and JSON/RAW conversion), the claim is only partially supported by the combined evidence. Specifically, S1 supports the first half, S2 supports the second half, but neither source supports the entire claim in its entirety as a unified description of a single method's strengths. The claim implies a single method has all these traits, but the evidence presents two different approaches (S1: Legacy/CPU-convert, S2: Shader/GPU-friendly). Therefore, it is partial.
